# InkOS — Boldteq Pattern Library Reference Brief

**Purpose:** Dense, actionable reference for building InkOS (tattoo studio management SaaS — multi-tenant, multi-artist). Every line is load-bearing. No marketing pages; pure authenticated app.

---

## 1. Stack Spec — `stacks/saas-nextjs-supabase-railway.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Next.js **16.2.3** (App Router only, `output: 'standalone'`), React 19, TypeScript 5.6+ with `strict: true`, zero `any`. Framework is locked — no deviation without Yash approval.
- Package manager: **pnpm 9.x** only. Node 20 LTS pinned in `.nvmrc` + `engines`. `packageManager` field locks pnpm.
- Auth: **`@supabase/ssr`** only — `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` is deprecated and banned. `getUser()` always, never `getSession()` for auth checks.
- Billing: **Dodo Payments** only (`@dodopayments/node`, `@dodopayments/web`). Webhook handler at `app/api/webhooks/dodo/route.ts`. Use `@dodopayments/nextjs` `Webhooks()` helper.
- Background work: **BullMQ + Redis** as separate Railway services. Next.js web service never blocks on async jobs. IORedis connection must have `maxRetriesPerRequest: null`.
- Folder roots that matter: `app/(auth)/`, `app/(app)/` (authenticated, sidebar in `layout.tsx`), `app/api/webhooks/dodo/`, `lib/supabase/{client,server,middleware,types}.ts`, `lib/dodo/client.ts`, `workers/jobs/`, `workers/cron/`, `supabase/migrations/`.

**Forbidden:**
- Vercel, Stripe, NextAuth.js, Prisma, Drizzle, any ORM, Pages Router, CSS modules/styled-components, npm/yarn, custom Express servers, self-hosted Postgres, MongoDB, AWS Lambda, `any` types, `console.log` in production code.

**Reusable path references:**
- `lib/supabase/server.ts` — server component client (async `cookies()`)
- `lib/supabase/middleware.ts` — session refresh on every request
- `lib/rate-limit.ts` — Upstash sliding window
- `lib/logger.ts` — pino structured logger
- `lib/queue.ts` — BullMQ Queue enqueuer (web service side)
- `app/api/health/route.ts` — Railway healthcheck (required)
- `app/api/webhooks/dodo/route.ts` — billing webhook handler
- `workers/jobs/index.ts` — BullMQ worker entry point
- `workers/cron/index.ts` — node-cron scheduler

---

## 2. UI/UX Production Standards — `patterns/good/ui-ux-production-standards.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- **Build order:** Phase 1 = full UI shell with placeholder/static data on every page. Phase 2 = wire Supabase. Phase 3 = billing, integrations, polish. Never skip Phase 1.
- Authenticated shell layout: `SidebarLayout` wraps all authenticated pages. Sidebar `w-56`. Content `flex-1 overflow-y-auto`. Every page has title + actions at top, then content cards/tables.
- Page title class is `text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight`. Stats numbers use `tabular-nums`. Never `text-xl font-semibold` for page titles — looks dated.
- Every mutation (create/update/delete) shows a sonner `toast.success`/`toast.error`. Error toasts include the message. Never `alert()`.
- Staggered list animations require `animationFillMode: "both"` — omitting it causes a visible pre-animation flash.
- Empty states on every list/table: icon + heading + description + action CTA. Distinct empty state for first-time-use vs. filtered-no-results. No "No data" alone.

**Forbidden:**
- Gradient hero sections, Lorem ipsum anywhere, buttons without loading states, hover-reveal action buttons (`opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` — breaks touch), hardcoded colors, `setTimeout` for loading, `alert()`/`console.log` for user feedback, card grids for data-heavy list pages (use data tables), custom CSS when Tailwind class exists.

**Reusable patterns:**
- `components/app/` — app-specific components (data tables, CRUD dialogs, stats cards, form sections)
- `components/ui/` — shadcn primitives (via CLI only)
- Sonner toast patterns: `toast.success("X created")`, `toast.error(error.message)`

---

## 3. Admin Panel Standards — `patterns/good/admin-panel-standards.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Admin at `/admin`. Single-page pattern: `AdminHeader` + `AdminSidebar` + `AdminErrorBoundary` keyed to `activeSection`. Each tab isolated with its own error boundary — one tab crash never kills the whole admin.
- Sidebar is 2-level max, grouped: OVERVIEW / USERS & BILLING / CONFIGURATION / SYSTEM. For InkOS: adapt groups to OVERVIEW / STUDIOS & ARTISTS / BILLING & PLANS / SYSTEM.
- The `sectionComponents` record is typed as `Record<AdminSection, React.ComponentType>` — each section is a lazy-loaded tab component.
- Dashboard tab: 4-6 KPI cards, user signups chart, MRR chart, system health indicators. Date-range picker required on all charts (7/30/90d + custom).
- Users tab: server-side pagination at 25/page, search on email+name (debounced 300ms), filters by role/status/plan, `...` menu with Edit/Ban/GDPR Export/Delete-with-type-confirm. Every admin action writes to `admin_audit_logs`.
- Desktop-first responsive: sidebar 250px sticky on 1200px+; drawer/hamburger on tablet; card-stacked tables on mobile.

**Forbidden:**
- Single error boundary wrapping entire admin (cascading failure). Admin sidebar built with different component stack than user sidebar.

**Reusable path references:**
- `components/app/admin/AdminHeader.tsx`, `AdminSidebar.tsx`, `AdminErrorBoundary.tsx`
- `lib/audit.ts` — `logAuditAction(who, what, whom, details)` helper

---

## 4. Sidebar Patterns — `patterns/good/sidebar-patterns.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Always use `shadcn Sidebar` + `SidebarProvider` + `SidebarContent` + `SidebarFooter` + `SidebarInset`. Never custom `<aside>` — you lose cookie-state persistence, mobile sheet drawer, icon-mode tooltips, and keyboard accessibility.
- Collapsed state styling: use `group-data-[collapsible=icon]:*` CSS classes only — never `useSidebar().state` ternaries in markup. CSS approach has zero re-renders; JS state causes flash because state update is synchronous but CSS transition is not.
- Active state icon: `text-white` (not `text-primary`) when background is the primary color — `text-primary` on `bg-primary` renders invisible.
- No duplicate nav: each destination appears in exactly one place (sidebar OR topbar dropdown, not both). Admin panel link: topbar dropdown only.
- Orphan separators: gate `<Separator>` with the same condition as the adjacent conditional element or it renders as a floating line.
- Icon size override: `!h-[18px] !w-[18px] shrink-0` to beat SidebarMenuButton's `[&>svg]:size-4` specificity.

**Forbidden:**
- Custom `<aside>` sidebar. `useSidebar()` state ternaries in markup for collapsed styling. `bg-primary/8` (invalid Tailwind — use `/10` or `/[0.08]`). Duplicate nav items.

**Reusable path references:**
- `components/ui/sidebar.tsx` — shadcn Sidebar system (install via CLI)
- `app/(app)/layout.tsx` — `SidebarProvider` + `Sidebar` + `SidebarInset` for all authenticated routes

---

## 5. Layout & Navigation Consistency — `patterns/good/layout-navigation-consistency.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- The `app/(app)/layout.tsx` route group automatically wraps ALL child pages with sidebar + header. New pages get sidebar for free — no per-page wrapper required (Next.js layout system enforces this).
- Every page falls into exactly one category: Authenticated (sidebar+header), Admin (AdminSidebar+AdminRoute), or Public (no sidebar). If unsure → Authenticated.
- When adding any new page, four things happen atomically in the same commit: create page file, add route (already done by Next.js file system), add sidebar nav item with correct path and icon, verify active state.
- Mobile sidebar trigger (`SidebarTrigger`) must be inside `SidebarInset` in the header area — without it, mobile users have no way to open sidebar.
- `AppHeader` lives inside `SidebarInset`, not outside — placing it outside breaks the flex layout.

**Forbidden:**
- Pages outside the `(app)/` route group without explicit reason. Missing `SidebarTrigger` on mobile. Dead sidebar links (route registered but nav item missing, or vice versa).

**Route group structure for InkOS:**
```
app/
  (auth)/layout.tsx           — centered, no sidebar
  (auth)/login/page.tsx
  (auth)/signup/page.tsx
  (app)/layout.tsx            — SidebarProvider + Sidebar + SidebarInset (all authenticated)
  (app)/dashboard/page.tsx
  (app)/bookings/...
  (app)/calendar/...
  (app)/clients/...
  (app)/artists/...
  (app)/inventory/...
  (app)/payroll/...
  (app)/settings/...
  admin/layout.tsx            — AdminSidebar
  admin/page.tsx
```

---

## 6. SaaS Winning Patterns — `patterns/good/saas-winning-patterns.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Speed is the product: button click <50ms (optimistic UI), page nav <100ms (prefetch on hover), form submit <200ms. Use skeleton loaders that match real layout (prevents CLS), not spinners. Never defer perceived performance to "nice to have."
- Every mutation is optimistic: update local QueryClient state immediately, sync to server in background, rollback with `context.previous` on error. Users should never wait for a server round-trip to see their action reflected.
- Command palette (Cmd+K with `cmdk`) required for power users. G+S = go to settings, G+D = go to dashboard. N = new item, E = edit. For InkOS: N = new booking, G+C = go to calendar.
- Every data-dependent component ships all 6 states: LOADING (skeleton), EMPTY (icon + CTA), ERROR (what went wrong + retry), SUCCESS, PARTIAL (pagination), OFFLINE (cached + indicator).
- Defaults beat customization. Ship one strong default for booking flow, consent form, commission split. Power users access overrides in Advanced. Never ship a Tier 3 option (you don't need it).
- Viral mechanic for InkOS: booking confirmation page is public-shareable (client shares tattoo appointment/design preview) → recipient sees InkOS brand.

**Forbidden:**
- "Let users decide" settings without a strong default. Feature-bolted-on referral badges. Spinners instead of skeletons. Blocking core workflow with upgrade prompts.

---

## 7. SaaS Growth & Onboarding — `patterns/good/saas-growth-onboarding.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Time-to-first-value < 2 minutes. For InkOS (studio owner signup): first action = create first booking or import first client in under 2 minutes. Pre-seed demo data on signup (sample artist, sample appointment).
- Signup form: 3 fields max (studio name, email, password). Every additional field = -7% completion. Gather intent (# of artists, # of locations) AFTER first login, not before.
- Onboarding checklist: 3-5 items. First item completable in <30 seconds (e.g., "Create your first booking"). Items 4-5 skippable. Progress bar persists across sessions. 6+ items drop below 30% completion.
- Progressive disclosure: Week 0 = core booking workflow only. Week 1 = reveal consent forms, client CRM. Week 2+ = payroll, commission splits, AI design assistant, guest artists.
- Intent routing at signup: ask "How many artists at your studio?" (1/2-5/6-20/20+) → routes to solo-artist onboarding vs. multi-artist studio onboarding vs. multi-location.
- In-app messages outperform email 3x for retention. Feature adoption of 5+ features = 3x lower churn. DAU >40% = 67% lower churn. Track these from day 1 via PostHog.

**Forbidden:**
- Blank dashboard after signup. Multi-screen setup wizard before first value. Email-verify gate blocking first session. Overwhelming navigation with all 20 InkOS sections on day 1.

---

## 8. Auth Patterns — `patterns/good/auth-patterns.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Auth is day-one infrastructure: data model (studio → artist → permissions → features) must exist before any feature code. Every API route protected by default; public routes are explicit opt-ins.
- Always `getUser()`, never `getSession()` in Server Components and API routes — `getSession()` does not validate the JWT against Supabase.
- Middleware at `middleware.ts` calls `getUser()` on every request to keep tokens refreshed and redirect unauthenticated users. Matcher excludes `_next/static`, `_next/image`, `favicon.ico`, and `api/webhooks`.
- Multi-tenant RBAC: roles stored on `studio_members` junction table (not on user). Hierarchy: `owner > admin > artist > receptionist`. Check permissions server-side in API route; UI hides elements but server enforces independently.
- Org-scoped RLS pattern: `USING (studio_id IN (SELECT studio_id FROM studio_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid()))`. For InkOS: studios are tenants, artists are members.
- Rate limits on auth endpoints: login 5/min, signup 3/min, reset 2/min. Account lockout after 10 failed attempts (30-min cooldown).

**Forbidden:**
- Tokens in localStorage (XSS exposed immediately). Auth tokens in URL query params (leaked in referrer). Trusting client-sent user/studio IDs — always derive from server session. Permissions checked only in UI. Shared service role keys across environments.

**Reusable path references:**
- `lib/supabase/server.ts` — `createClient()` for Server Components + Route Handlers
- `lib/supabase/client.ts` — `createClient()` for Client Components only
- `middleware.ts` — token refresh + protected route redirect

## 9. Billing Patterns — `patterns/good/billing-patterns.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Billing is day-one architecture. InkOS `subscriptions` table: `studio_id, dodo_subscription_id, dodo_customer_id, plan_id, status CHECK ('active','trialing','past_due','canceled'), current_period_start, current_period_end, cancel_at_period_end`. Only service role writes to this table (webhook handler); studios read their own row.
- Webhook handler uses `@dodopayments/nextjs` `Webhooks()` helper. Validate `x-dodo-signature` with `timingSafeEqual` before any DB write. Zod-parse the event shape — reject malformed webhooks with 400. Use `standardwebhooks` for Deno/Edge Functions.
- Customer portal: `GET https://api.dodopayments.com/customers/{id}/portal` → redirect to returned link. No custom billing UI needed.
- No `VITE_DODO_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` or any frontend-exposed Dodo key — Dodo has no frontend SDK. All calls are server-side.
- Grace period on payment failure: 3-7 days, not instant cutoff. Cancellation: preserve data, restrict features, show upgrade prompt. Never delete data on cancellation.
- Feature gating server-side only: check `subscription.plan` in API route/Server Action, return 403 with `{ requiredPlan: 'pro' }` body. UI shows upgrade prompt; server enforces.

**Forbidden:**
- Custom payment card forms (PCI nightmare — use Dodo Checkout hosted pages). Checking subscription status only in UI. Hard-coding prices (use Dodo product IDs). Deleting user data on cancellation. Skipping trial periods on new signups.

**Env vars (server-side only, never `NEXT_PUBLIC_`):**
- `DODO_API_KEY`, `DODO_PAYMENTS_WEBHOOK_KEY` (format: `whsec_...`), `DODO_PRODUCT_{PLAN}_{CYCLE}`

## 10. Supabase Database Mastery — `patterns/good/supabase-database-mastery.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Every table follows the standard template: `id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`, `studio_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, `created_at/updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, RLS enabled, `set_updated_at` trigger, index on every FK.
- RLS performance: avoid subqueries in every-row checks. Use a `SECURITY DEFINER STABLE` function that returns `uuid[]` and cache via `auth.user_studio_ids()` — then policy becomes `WHERE studio_id = ANY(auth.user_studio_ids())`. Index `studio_members(user_id)`.
- Use CHECK constraints for status/type enums, NOT Postgres ENUM types — ENUM can't remove values and is a migration nightmare.
- Migration naming: `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql`. Always `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`. Never `ALTER COLUMN SET NOT NULL` without a default — use `NOT VALID` check constraint then `VALIDATE`.
- `subscriptions` table: only service role writes (webhook), studio reads own row. `audit_log` table: only service role reads.
- Use port 6543 (pooled/Supavisor) for application queries. Port 5432 (direct) for migrations only.

**Forbidden:**
- Postgres ENUM types (use CHECK constraints). `CREATE INDEX` without CONCURRENTLY (locks table). Renaming columns directly (expand-migrate-contract pattern instead). Any public table missing RLS — Sage blocks deploy.

**Reusable path references:**
- `supabase/migrations/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_bootstrap.sql` — first migration with `studios`, `studio_members`, `profiles`, RLS, triggers
- `lib/supabase/types.ts` — generated via `pnpm supabase gen types typescript --linked` (regenerate after every migration)
- `public.handle_updated_at()` trigger function — create once, apply to all tables
- `public.handle_new_user()` trigger — auto-create `profiles` row on `auth.users` insert

## 11. shadcn base-nova Patterns — `patterns/good/shadcn-base-nova-patterns.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- base-nova uses `render` prop, NOT `asChild`. Detection rule: if component imports from `@base-ui/react` → use `render`. If from `@radix-ui/*` → use `asChild`. Always grep before assuming. `<SidebarMenuButton render={<Link href="/x" />}>Dashboard</SidebarMenuButton>`.
- Tailwind v4: no `tailwind.config.ts`. All custom tokens (`--shadow-soft`, `--shadow-card`, `--shadow-soft-md`, keyframes) go in `app/globals.css` under `@theme inline`. Any pattern doc referencing a JS config file is stale for v4.
- Sidebar active state: CSS selector in `globals.css` targeting `[data-sidebar="menu-button"][data-active="true"]`, not JS state ternaries — Sage flags the ternary approach as a hard fail.
- Settings tabs that are real routes: use `Link` + `usePathname`, not `<Tabs>` component. Active indicator: `after:absolute after:inset-x-0 after:-bottom-px after:h-0.5 after:bg-primary`.
- Dark mode: explicitly override `--primary` in `.dark` to keep brand hue (default shadcn dark sets it near-white, destroying brand color).
- Data tables with active filters: pass both `rows={filteredRows}` and `totalCount={allRows.length}` — footer shows "Showing 12 of 47" not "12 of 12".

**Forbidden (Sage hard fails):**
- `any`/`@ts-ignore`. Raw hex color anywhere except one designated brand swatch. `console.log`. `TODO` comments (except explicit phase markers). `useSidebar()` state ternaries in markup. `asChild` on base-nova components. Default Tailwind `shadow-sm`/`shadow-md` (use `shadow-soft*`/`shadow-card`). Routes returning non-200/307/404.

**Reusable path references:**
- `app/globals.css` — `@theme inline` block for all custom tokens, Vega owns
- `lib/design-tokens.ts` — Vega owns

## 12. Competitive Dominance Engine — `patterns/good/competitive-dominance-engine.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Eight moats: Speed, Keyboard-first UX, Complete Feature States, Design Quality, Onboarding Conversion, Viral Mechanics, Domain-specific AI (not ChatGPT wrapper), Production Infrastructure. Every feature must address all 8.
- For InkOS AI: context-aware (knows artist's style portfolio, client history, past designs), not generic chat. Auto-generates consent form suggestions based on tattoo type. Predictive: "Your Friday slots fill by Tuesday — want to auto-close Thursday bookings?"
- Cmd+K command palette required. InkOS shortcuts: N = new booking, G+C = calendar, G+CL = clients, G+A = artists.
- Domination metric targets: P95 interaction <100ms, activation (day 1) >60%, DAU/MAU >40%, monthly churn <2%, NPS >60, feature adoption 5+ features by day 30, referral rate >20%.
- Design quality: 4px grid (everything divisible by 4), max 3 font sizes per page, semantic colors only (no hardcoded hex), every state transition animated at 150ms ease-out minimum.

**Forbidden:**
- Generic "AI assistant" chat interface. Bolted-on referral badges. Spinner instead of layout-matched skeleton. Missing any of the 6 feature states on any data-dependent component.

## 13. Stack A Scaffold Dry Run — `patterns/good/stack-a-scaffold-dryrun.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Next.js 16 renamed `middleware.ts` to `proxy.ts`. The `@supabase/ssr` `createServerClient` `cookies()` adapter must be awaited (`await cookies()`). `updateSession` must rewrite cookies on BOTH the request (for downstream reads) AND the response (for browser to send next time).
- Supabase integration files live at `src/integrations/supabase/{browser,server,middleware}.ts` OR `lib/supabase/{client,server,middleware}.ts` — pick one convention and never mix.
- Dodo webhook: HMAC-SHA256 + `timingSafeEqual` on `x-dodo-signature`. Zod-parse the event body. Never trust `metadata.profile_id` (or `metadata.studio_id` for InkOS) without verifying signature first.
- BullMQ worker: separate `package.json`, plain Node, no `next/*` imports. Service-role Supabase client (not anon). `maxRetriesPerRequest: null` on IORedis. SIGTERM graceful shutdown required.
- Sentry Next 16: both `instrumentation.ts` AND `instrumentation-client.ts` required. Missing `instrumentation-client.ts` is the #1 "client errors not in Sentry" bug.
- RLS gate (Sage runs pre-deploy): every public table must have RLS enabled + at least one policy. Two-query SQL check — both must return empty results.

**Forbidden:**
- `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` import anywhere. `VITE_` prefixed vars in a Next.js project. `console.log` in `app/` or `src/`. Non-awaited `cookies()` in server components. Workers importing `from 'next/...'`.

**Reusable path references:**
- `proxy.ts` (root) — replaces `middleware.ts` in Next 16
- `instrumentation.ts` + `instrumentation-client.ts` — both required for Sentry
- `app/api/dodo/webhook/route.ts` — scaffold pattern with `timingSafeEqual` + Zod

## 14. Next.js Production Infra — `patterns/good/nextjs-production-infra.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Env vars validated on boot with Zod in `lib/env.ts` — app crashes loudly if any required var is missing. `DODO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` must `.startsWith('whsec_')`, `RESEND_API_KEY` must `.startsWith('re_')`.
- Three rate-limit tiers in `lib/rate-limit.ts`: `apiRatelimit` (10 req/10s per IP for public), `authedRatelimit` (60 req/min per user), `expensiveRatelimit` (token bucket 5/min for AI endpoints). Return `X-RateLimit-*` headers on 429.
- Three cache layers: Layer 1 = `unstable_cache` with `revalidateTag` (server DB queries, 60s TTL). Layer 2 = Upstash Redis for cross-request shared data. Layer 3 = TanStack Query client-side (`staleTime: 60_000`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`).
- Storage buckets: `public-assets` (CDN, public URLs), `user-uploads` (RLS-gated, signed URLs, 1hr expiry), `temp` (auto-delete via cron after 24h). RLS on storage objects: `auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]`.
- Security headers in `next.config.ts`: CSP, HSTS (`max-age=63072000`), `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. CSP `connect-src` must include `https://api.dodopayments.com`.
- Every API route: validate input with Zod (`.safeParse`, return `400` with `error.format()` on failure).

**Forbidden:**
- Unvalidated env vars (silent undefined bugs). Missing security headers. Uploading files without MIME validation. Triggering expensive operations (AI, billing) without the `expensiveRatelimit` tier. Direct prod migrations without staging validation.

**Reusable path references:**
- `lib/env.ts` — Zod boot-time validation
- `lib/rate-limit.ts` — three rate-limit tiers
- `lib/cache.ts` — `cacheGet`/`cacheSet`/`cacheBust` (Upstash Redis wrapper)
- `lib/queue.ts` — BullMQ Queue enqueuer with `attempts: 3, backoff: exponential`
- `app/api/health/route.ts` + `_health` migration — Railway healthcheck protocol

## 15. Railway Deployment — `patterns/good/railway-deployment.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Railway project shape: 4 services per environment (`web`, `worker-jobs`, `worker-cron`, `redis`). Preview environments are lighter (`web` + `redis` only, job queue disabled). Production and staging always mirror each other.
- All services communicate via Railway private networking (`REDIS_PRIVATE_URL` = `${{redis.REDIS_PRIVATE_URL}}`, `redis.railway.internal:6379`). Never use public URLs between Railway services — billable egress and slower.
- `railway.toml` at repo root: `builder = "NIXPACKS"`, `buildCommand = "pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build"`, `healthcheckPath = "/api/health"`, `restartPolicyType = "ON_FAILURE"`. Each worker has its own `[[services]]` entry with `source` pointing to worker directory.
- Auto-rollback triggers (Hawk monitors 15 min post-deploy): error rate >1% for 5 min, healthcheck non-200 for 3 consecutive checks, P95 latency >2s for 5 min, Sentry new-error spike >10 in 5 min.
- Env vars per-environment via `railway variables set`. Local dev pulls staging vars via `railway variables pull --environment staging > .env.local`. Secrets never in `.env.example` — placeholders only.
- Preview URL pattern for testing: `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL=$PREVIEW_URL pnpm test:e2e`. Supabase branching enabled per PR via `supabase/config.toml` `[experimental.branching] enabled = true`.

**Forbidden:**
- Manual `railway up` deploys (everything via GitHub push auto-deploy). Public internet between Railway services (private networking only). Production deploys without staging Sage+Luna pass. Missing `ROLLBACK.md` per project. Cloudflare proxied mode (DNS-only if used for DDoS).

**Reusable path references:**
- `railway.toml` — canonical config at repo root
- `workers/jobs/Dockerfile` + `workers/jobs/railway.toml` — per-worker deploy config

## 2. UI/UX Production Standards — `patterns/good/ui-ux-production-standards.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**

**Forbidden:**
- Gradient hero sections, Lorem ipsum anywhere, buttons without loading states, hover-reveal action buttons (`opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` — breaks touch), hardcoded colors, `setTimeout` for loading, `alert()`/`console.log` for user feedback, card grids for data-heavy list pages (use data tables), custom CSS when Tailwind class exists.

**Forbidden:**
- Single error boundary wrapping entire admin (cascading failure). Admin sidebar built with different component stack than user sidebar.

## 6. SaaS Winning Patterns — `patterns/good/saas-winning-patterns.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Speed is the product: button click <50ms (optimistic UI), page nav <100ms (prefetch on hover), form submit <200ms. Use skeleton loaders that match real layout (prevents CLS), not spinners. Never defer perceived performance to "nice to have."
- Every mutation is optimistic: update local QueryClient state immediately, sync to server in background, rollback with `context.previous` on error. Users should never wait for a server round-trip to see their action reflected.
- Command palette (Cmd+K with `cmdk`) required for power users. G+S = go to settings, G+D = go to dashboard. N = new item, E = edit. For InkOS: N = new booking, G+C = go to calendar.
- Every data-dependent component ships all 6 states: LOADING (skeleton), EMPTY (icon + CTA), ERROR (what went wrong + retry), SUCCESS, PARTIAL (pagination), OFFLINE (cached + indicator).
- Defaults beat customization. Ship one strong default for booking flow, consent form, commission split. Power users access overrides in Advanced. Never ship a Tier 3 option (you don't need it).
- Viral mechanic for InkOS: booking confirmation page is public-shareable (client shares tattoo appointment/design preview) → recipient sees InkOS brand.

**Forbidden:**
- "Let users decide" settings without a strong default. Feature-bolted-on referral badges. Spinners instead of skeletons. Blocking core workflow with upgrade prompts.

## 7. SaaS Growth & Onboarding — `patterns/good/saas-growth-onboarding.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Time-to-first-value < 2 minutes. For InkOS (studio owner signup): first action = create first booking or import first client in under 2 minutes. Pre-seed demo data on signup (sample artist, sample appointment).
- Signup form: 3 fields max (studio name, email, password). Every additional field = -7% completion. Gather intent (# of artists, # of locations) AFTER first login, not before.
- Onboarding checklist: 3-5 items. First item completable in <30 seconds (e.g., "Create your first booking"). Items 4-5 skippable. Progress bar persists across sessions. 6+ items drop below 30% completion.
- Progressive disclosure: Week 0 = core booking workflow only. Week 1 = reveal consent forms, client CRM. Week 2+ = payroll, commission splits, AI design assistant, guest artists.
- Intent routing at signup: ask "How many artists at your studio?" (1/2-5/6-20/20+) → routes to solo-artist onboarding vs. multi-artist studio onboarding vs. multi-location.
- In-app messages outperform email 3x for retention. Feature adoption of 5+ features = 3x lower churn. DAU >40% = 67% lower churn. Track these from day 1 via PostHog.

**Forbidden:**

## 8. Auth Patterns — `patterns/good/auth-patterns.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Auth is day-one infrastructure: data model (studio → artist → permissions → features) must exist before any feature code. Every API route protected by default; public routes are explicit opt-ins.
- Always `getUser()`, never `getSession()` in Server Components and API routes — `getSession()` does not validate the JWT against Supabase.
- Middleware at `middleware.ts` calls `getUser()` on every request to keep tokens refreshed and redirect unauthenticated users. Matcher excludes `_next/static`, `_next/image`, `favicon.ico`, and `api/webhooks`.
- Multi-tenant RBAC: roles stored on `studio_members` junction table (not on user). Hierarchy: `owner > admin > artist > receptionist`. Check permissions server-side in API route; UI hides elements but server enforces independently.
- Org-scoped RLS pattern: `USING (studio_id IN (SELECT studio_id FROM studio_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid()))`. For InkOS: studios are tenants, artists are members.
- Rate limits on auth endpoints: login 5/min, signup 3/min, reset 2/min. Account lockout after 10 failed attempts (30-min cooldown).

**Forbidden:**
- Tokens in localStorage (XSS exposed immediately). Auth tokens in URL query params (leaked in referrer). Trusting client-sent user/studio IDs — always derive from server session. Permissions checked only in UI. Shared service role keys across environments.

**Reusable path references:**
- `lib/supabase/server.ts` — `createClient()` for Server Components + Route Handlers

## 9. Billing Patterns — `patterns/good/billing-patterns.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Billing is day-one architecture. InkOS `subscriptions` table: `studio_id, dodo_subscription_id, dodo_customer_id, plan_id, status CHECK ('active','trialing','past_due','canceled'), current_period_start, current_period_end, cancel_at_period_end`. Only service role writes to this table (webhook handler); studios read their own row.

## 10. Supabase Database Mastery — `patterns/good/supabase-database-mastery.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Every table follows the standard template: `id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()`, `studio_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES studios(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, `created_at/updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, RLS enabled, `set_updated_at` trigger, index on every FK.
- RLS performance: avoid subqueries in every-row checks. Use a `SECURITY DEFINER STABLE` function that returns `uuid[]` and cache via `auth.user_studio_ids()` — then policy becomes `WHERE studio_id = ANY(auth.user_studio_ids())`. Index `studio_members(user_id)`.
- Use CHECK constraints for status/type enums, NOT Postgres ENUM types — ENUM can't remove values and is a migration nightmare.
- Migration naming: `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql`. Always `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`. Never `ALTER COLUMN SET NOT NULL` without a default — use `NOT VALID` check constraint then `VALIDATE`.
- `subscriptions` table: only service role writes (webhook), studio reads own row. `audit_log` table: only service role reads.
- Use port 6543 (pooled/Supavisor) for application queries. Port 5432 (direct) for migrations only.

**Forbidden:**
- Postgres ENUM types (use CHECK constraints). `CREATE INDEX` without CONCURRENTLY (locks table). Renaming columns directly (expand-migrate-contract pattern instead). Any public table missing RLS — Sage blocks deploy.

**Reusable path references:**
- `supabase/migrations/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_bootstrap.sql` — first migration with `studios`, `studio_members`, `profiles`, RLS, triggers
- `lib/supabase/types.ts` — generated via `pnpm supabase gen types typescript --linked` (regenerate after every migration)
- `public.handle_updated_at()` trigger function — create once, apply to all tables
- `public.handle_new_user()` trigger — auto-create `profiles` row on `auth.users` insert

## 15. Railway Deployment — `patterns/good/railway-deployment.md`

**Load-bearing rules:**
- Railway project shape: 4 services per environment (`web`, `worker-jobs`, `worker-cron`, `redis`). Preview environments are lighter (`web` + `redis` only, job queue disabled). Production and staging always mirror each other.

# InkOS — Production-Grade Tattoo Studio OS — Build Plan

## Context

InkOS is a vertical SaaS for tattoo studios — the operating system the industry has been waiting for. The dossier proves the niche is real, growing (10.6% CAGR), underserved by legacy tools (DaySmart UX is 2018-era, no AI anywhere), and high-ARPU (studios average $250K/yr revenue with 55% margins).

**Goal:** Ship a full v1 web app (no marketing site — pure authenticated SaaS) that makes every existing competitor look obsolete. Build every moat — AI design assistant, full payroll + 1099-K, guest artist module, multi-location, white-label — before launch. Target first paying studios in 20–24 weeks.

**Scope:** Authenticated web app only. Multi-tenant from migration #1. Multi-user (artists + owners + receptionists) from day 1. 4-tier pricing (Solo $29 / Studio $59 / Pro $99 / Enterprise $199).

**Working directory:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS` — currently empty. Greenfield.

---

## Strategic Positioning — How We Beat Each Competitor

| Competitor | Their Weakness | InkOS Counter |
|---|---|---|
| **DaySmart Body Art** | Stagnant product, broken consent printing, no payroll, dated UX | Modern UX + ship weekly + native digital consents + full payroll |
| **Tattoo Studio Pro** | No payroll, no AI, no guest artists | All three included in Pro tier at same price |
| **Porter** | $250/mo Studio Pro for 5 artists, US-only, no AI | $59 Studio tier covers 5 artists with commissions, global from day 1, AI included in Pro |
| **TattooGenda** | Poor English UX, no AI, max 10 artists | US-grade UX + EU REACH compliance + unlimited artists |
| **Fresha** | 20% marketplace commission, hidden fees, churn event in 2025 | Flat fee, zero commissions, transparent pricing — direct migration target |
| **Booksy** | Generic (barbers/spas/salons), no consent forms, no commissions | Tattoo-native by design |
| **TattooPro** | Opaque pricing, dated UX, no AI | Modern UX, public pricing, AI moat |

**Five durable moats:**
1. **AI Design Assistant** — Claude API generates moodboards from client style references pre-consultation. Zero competitors have this.
2. **Full payroll + 1099-K at $99 vs Porter's $250** — 4× cheaper for the same feature.
3. **EU REACH ink passports + GDPR-native** — only TattooGenda has this; we match it with US-grade UX.
4. **Transparent flat pricing** — Fresha's 2025 bait-and-switch created mass churn we capture.
5. **Guest artist module included at $99** — Porter only at $250, nobody else has it.

---

## Locked Architecture

**Stack A (LOCKED 2026-04-10):** Next.js 16.2.3 (App Router) + React 19 + TypeScript strict + Tailwind 4 + shadcn/ui (base-nova variant) + Supabase (auth/DB/storage) + Dodo Payments + Resend + Sentry + PostHog + Railway (web + workers + Redis) + pnpm + Node 20 LTS.

**Forbidden (Sage hard-fails on these):** Vercel, Stripe, NextAuth, Prisma, Pages Router, `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs`, `any`, `console.log`, npm/yarn, CSS modules, raw hex colors outside one brand swatch, `useSidebar()` ternaries in markup, `asChild` on base-nova components, default Tailwind `shadow-sm/md` (use `shadow-soft*`).

**Topology:** Next.js web service on Railway · separate `worker-jobs` and `worker-cron` Railway services · Supabase Postgres + Auth + Storage · Upstash Redis for queues + cache · Sentry + PostHog · Cloudflare DNS-only.

**Reference patterns to load on every sprint:**

- `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/executable-auto-fix-loop.md`

## Data Model (Multi-Tenant, RLS-Enforced)

`studio_id` is the tenant key on every domain table. RLS uses cached helper:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION auth.user_studio_ids()
RETURNS uuid[] LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER STABLE AS $$
  SELECT array_agg(studio_id) FROM public.studio_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid();
$$;
-- Index: studio_members(user_id) — required for performance
```

**Core tables (all with `id uuid PK`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `set_updated_at` trigger, RLS enabled, FK indexes):**

| Table | Tenant scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `profiles` | user-scoped | Auto-created via `handle_new_user()` trigger |
| `studios` | tenant root | name, slug, timezone, locale, currency, brand_color, logo_url, plan_id |
| `studio_members` | studio | user_id, role CHECK ('owner','admin','artist','receptionist','guest_artist') |
| `locations` | studio | multi-location support from day 1 |
| `artists` | studio | profile_id (nullable for non-user artists), bio, portfolio_url, commission_default_pct, status |
| `services` | studio | name, duration_min, base_price, deposit_pct, requires_consult |
| `clients` | studio | no auth — referenced by booking magic link |
| `client_notes` | studio | allergies, skin notes, medical, emergency_contact |
| `bookings` | studio | client_id, artist_id, service_id, location_id, scheduled_at, duration_min, status CHECK ('pending','confirmed','in_progress','completed','cancelled','no_show') |
| `booking_photos` | studio | bucket: design-assets, before/during/after |
| `consent_form_templates` | studio | sections jsonb (fields: text/sig/checkbox/upload), version |
| `consent_form_submissions` | studio | template_id, booking_id, signed_at, signature_data, ip, pdf_url |
| `inventory_items` | studio | sku, name, category, current_stock, low_stock_threshold, supplier_id |
| `inventory_movements` | studio | item_id, qty_delta, reason, booking_id (nullable) |
| `commission_rules` | studio | artist_id, service_id (nullable), percentage, flat_fee, effective_from |
| `commission_records` | studio | artist_id, booking_id, amount, status CHECK ('pending','approved','paid') |
| `payroll_runs` | studio | period_start/end, total_amount, status, generated_by |
| `payroll_artist_summary` | studio | run_id, artist_id, total_commissions, total_tips, net_amount |

**RLS pattern (every domain table):**
```sql
ALTER TABLE bookings ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "tenant_read" ON bookings FOR SELECT
  USING (studio_id = ANY(auth.user_studio_ids()));
CREATE POLICY "tenant_write" ON bookings FOR INSERT
  WITH CHECK (studio_id = ANY(auth.user_studio_ids()));
-- Plus role-restricted policies for payroll, commission_rules, tax_forms (owner+admin only)
```

**Public client booking flow:** Bookings table has a separate Pattern C policy — public read via `booking_token` (UUID) for client-facing confirmation/consent pages, no auth required.

## Sidebar Information Architecture

## Feature Delivery — 12 Sprints × 2 weeks = 24 Weeks

Each sprint = 2 weeks. Validation gate (Sage + Luna) at end of every sprint. Rex orchestrates; Vega designs before Koda builds; Dato owns every migration.

### Sprint 0 — Scaffold & Foundations (Week 1–2)
- Riko scaffolds Stack A: Next.js 16.2.3, Tailwind 4, shadcn base-nova, Supabase, Dodo, Resend, Sentry, PostHog, Railway 4-service topology (web + worker-jobs + worker-cron + redis).

### Sprint 2 — Booking Engine + Calendar (Week 5–6)
- Migration: `services`, `bookings`, `clients`, `client_notes`, `booking_photos`.
- Calendar view: day/week/month with drag-drop reschedule (FullCalendar React or react-big-calendar — Vega picks).
- Appointment CRUD with deposit collection placeholder (Dodo wired in Sprint 4).
- Public booking page at `/book/[studioSlug]` — service picker, calendar slot picker, client info form, deposit prompt.
- Conflict detection: artist double-booking prevented at DB level via `EXCLUDE USING gist` constraint.
- Magic-link confirmation email via Resend → public `/book/.../confirmation/[token]` page.

### Sprint 3 — Clients CRM + Photo History (Week 7–8)
- Client list (data table with search, tag filter, sort by last visit / total spend).
- Client detail page: profile, intake notes, full session history, photo gallery (before/during/after), upcoming/past appointments, total spend.
- Photo upload via Supabase Storage with MIME validation, 10MB limit, signed URLs.
- Tag system: studio defines tags (VIP, allergic, healing-issues), client gets multiple.
- "We miss you" inactive-client query: clients with no booking in 90 days.

### Sprint 4 — Payments via Dodo + Deposits (Week 9–10)
- Dodo Payments products created: 4 plans × 2 cycles = 8 products. Webhook handler at `app/api/webhooks/dodo/route.ts` with `timingSafeEqual` + Zod parse + idempotency via `webhook_events`.
- Subscription lifecycle: trial → active → past_due → canceled. `subscriptions` table updated only by webhook. Customer portal redirect for self-service.
- Deposit collection on booking: Dodo hosted checkout, captured at booking, refundable via cancellation policy.
- Server-side feature gating: `requireFeature(plan, 'ai_design')` returns 403 with `{ requiredPlan: 'pro' }`.
- Settings → Billing page: current plan, usage meters, upgrade/downgrade, invoice history.

### Sprint 5 — Digital Consent Forms (Week 11–12)
- Migration: `consent_form_templates`, `consent_form_submissions`.
- Template builder: drag-drop section editor (text, signature, checkbox, file upload, dropdown). Versioning per template.
- Public consent flow at `/book/.../consent/[token]`: render template, signature pad (touch + mouse + stylus), IP + timestamp + user agent capture.
- PDF generation via worker job (`generate-consent-pdf`) using `@react-pdf/renderer`, stored in RLS-protected bucket `consent-forms`. Auto-emailed to client + artist.
- Bulk template library seeded: general tattoo, piercing, PMU, touch-up, minor consent.
- GDPR data retention: configurable per studio (default 7 years), auto-delete worker.

### Sprint 6 — Artist Profiles + Schedules + Multi-User (Week 13–14)
- Artist invite flow: owner invites by email → magic link signup → joins `studio_members` as `artist`.
- Artist self-view: their own calendar only, their clients only, their commission balance only (RLS enforces).
- Schedule editor: weekly availability, blocked dates, vacation, recurring slots.
- Receptionist role: can manage bookings + clients but not commissions, payroll, or settings.
- Team & Roles page in settings: invite, role change, deactivate (preserves data).

### Sprint 7 — Commissions Engine (Week 15–16)
- Migration: `commission_rules`, `commission_records`.
- Per-artist + per-service commission rules with effective dates and audit trail.
- Auto-calculation on booking status → `completed`: insert into `commission_records` as `pending`.
- Commissions page: per-artist running totals, approval workflow (owner approves → status `approved`).
- Tip handling: optional tip prompt on completion; tips bypass commission split (100% to artist by default, configurable).
- Discrepancy alerts: any commission record older than 30 days unapproved → dashboard alert.

### Sprint 8 — Payroll + 1099-K + Tax Compliance (Week 17–18)
- Migration: `payroll_runs`, `payroll_artist_summary`, `tax_forms`.
- Monthly payroll runs (cron 1st of month): aggregates approved commissions + tips per artist, generates `payroll_artist_summary`.
- Owner approves run → status `paid`, optional CSV/QuickBooks export, optional Dodo Connect payout (deferred to v1.1 if Dodo doesn't support).
- W-9 collection via secure form (encrypted at rest, accessible owner+admin only).
- 1099-K generation cron (Jan 15 of each year): aggregates prior year payments per artist, generates PDF via worker, stores in `tax-forms` bucket, emails artist.
- US tax thresholds and EU VAT-compliant invoicing.

### Sprint 9 — AI Design Assistant (Week 19–20)
- Migration: `ai_design_requests`, `ai_design_outputs`.
- Pre-consultation form on client portal: style preference, body area, reference image uploads, budget, notes.
- Anthropic Claude API integration via worker job `process-ai-design`. NEVER on web service. `expensiveRatelimit` (5/min per user). Token + cost logging per studio for billing visibility.
- Prompt chain: analyze references → generate detailed moodboard description → image generation via Stable Diffusion API or DALL-E 3 (Vega picks based on cost + quality).
- Artist review screen: approve/reject/iterate, add notes, send to client. Version history per request.
- Style tagging system (blackwork, watercolor, traditional, neo-trad, realism, geometric, minimalist) feeds artist matching.
- Hard-gated to Pro tier ($99). Usage cap: 100 generations/mo on Pro, unlimited on Enterprise. Studios can buy 50-pack add-ons.
- Cost monitoring in admin panel — auto-throttle if studio exceeds 2× expected usage.

### Sprint 10 — Inventory + Guest Artist Module (Week 21–22)
**Inventory:**
- Items catalog: inks (brand, color, ML), needles, cartridges, aftercare retail.
- Stock movements logged per session (auto-decrement on session close), low-stock email/SMS alerts.
- Per-location inventory with transfer workflow.
- Suppliers + purchase orders.

**Guest Artists:**
- Migration: `guest_artist_engagements`.
- Invite flow: studio owner invites guest artist with start/end dates and custom split %.
- Guest artist gets temp `guest_artist` role on `studio_members`, auto-revoked on `end_date` via cron.
- Guest artist sees their own calendar only at this studio. Bookings tagged as guest engagement for separate revenue tracking.
- Public booking page shows guest artist availability during their stay.

### Sprint 11 — Multi-Location + White-Label + Marketing Automation (Week 23–24)
**Multi-location:**
- Sidebar gains "Locations" group when `count(locations) > 1`.
- Per-location dashboards with rollup view at studio level.
- Centralized client + artist roster, with per-location assignments.
- Per-location service catalog override.

**White-label (Enterprise tier):**
- Custom domain CNAME for booking page (`book.mystudio.com` instead of `book.inkos.app/[slug]`).
- Custom logo, color palette, favicon on client-facing pages.
- Remove all "Powered by InkOS" branding from client pages.
- Custom email "from" name + reply-to.

**Marketing automation:**

The spec is written. Here is what was produced and why each decision was made:

**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS/.handoffs/sprint-1-design-spec.md`

---

**Key design decisions locked in:**

**Auth pages.** Max-w-[400px] centered card with a 3px electric-purple top edge and a `radial-gradient` at `opacity-[0.07]` in the layout background. This distinguishes it from generic SaaS (no hero image, no marketing copy, just the tool) while signaling the brand immediately. The auth layout gets the glow added to `(auth)/layout.tsx`.

**Signup — 3 fields only.** Studio name + email + password. No phone, no company size, no "how did you hear about us". Every extra field drops completion 7%. The `handle_new_user` trigger already seeds the studio record, so no extra step needed.

**Sidebar active state.** Pure CSS: `[data-sidebar="menu-button"][data-active="true"]` in globals.css. No `useSidebar()` ternaries. The active color is `oklch(75% 0.18 292)` (lighter purple) on a `oklch(62% 0.24 292 / 0.12)` background — visible against the dark sidebar without being neon-harsh. Icon inherits the same color via the `svg` selector. This addresses the "purple on purple = invisible" antipattern from sidebar-patterns.md directly.

**Role-aware nav.** Filtered server-side before the component receives it — not hidden with CSS. This prevents layout flicker and avoids leaking nav item text to artists via DOM inspection.

**Dashboard bottom row.** Schedule timeline spans 2/3 width at `md+` with activity feed and alerts in the remaining 1/3. On mobile everything stacks. The 6 KPI cards are `grid-cols-4` at `lg` but the 6th card wraps to a new row naturally — avoids an odd 5+1 layout.

**`animationFillMode: "both"` is hard-coded in every stagger example.** This was flagged as a production bug across multiple projects in the base-nova patterns file — cards flash their final state before animation starts without it.

**Token additions are minimal and additive.** The existing `globals.css` already has the full color system, shadows, radius, and sidebar tokens. The additions are: status colors for booking lifecycle, neon-purple glow for the step-5 success icon, animation keyframes (fade-in-up, fade-in, slide-in-right), and the component CSS layer for active sidebar state + status badges.

**Onboarding step 5** fires a PostHog `onboarding_completed` event with duration so the TTV metric is measurable from day 1. The "What's next" list pre-loads the mental model for Sprint 2 features without requiring any UI to back it yet.
